credit_metrics.text: EBITDA rose by {{ebitda.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda@FY2024}}, well short of the {{revenue.change@FY2024}} revenue growth, so operating profit fell by {{operating_profit.change@FY2024}} to {{operating_profit@FY2024}}.
Total debt increased by {{total_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{total_debt@FY2024}}, yet gross leverage eased to {{gross_leverage@FY2024}} from {{gross_leverage@FY2023}}.
Interest coverage improved to {{interest_coverage@FY2024}}, but FFO to debt was stable at {{ffo_to_debt@FY2024}} and FCF to debt fell by {{fcf_to_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2024}}.
Capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2024}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2024}}, which absorbed most of the cash generated and left free cash flow at {{fcf@FY2024}}.

liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments fell by {{cash_like.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_like@FY2024}}, and cash liquidity moved with them to {{cash_liquidity@FY2024}}.
Cash liquidity to revenue declined by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}}, a thinner buffer against the group's debt service.
The group raised bond funding in May 2024, whose proceeds feature among the year's cash flows.

operating_performance.text: The Paris airports handled {{passengers@FY2024}} passengers in FY2024, while group revenue reached {{revenue@FY2024}} on the wider perimeter that includes TAV Airports and the international airports.
The group extended its Extime retail offering beyond Paris airports with the acquisition of Paris Experience Group and P/S in October 2024.
Following the merger of GMR Airports Infrastructures Ltd and GMR Airports Ltd, the group holds a lower economic interest in GMR Airports.
DIAL filed its tariff proposal for the next Delhi regulatory period, with final tariffs published later and effective in April 2025.

peer_positioning.text: Groupe ADP has the weakest EBITDA margin of the airport peers ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@2024}}), at {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}} against a median of {{ebitda_margin.peer_median@2024}}.
Gross leverage of {{gross_leverage@FY2024}} is above the peer median of {{gross_leverage.peer_median@2024}} and ranks {{gross_leverage.peer_rank@2024}}.

Interest coverage of {{interest_coverage@FY2024}} and FFO to debt of {{ffo_to_debt@FY2024}} both sit below the peer medians of {{interest_coverage.peer_median@2024}} and {{ffo_to_debt.peer_median@2024}}.
FCF to debt of {{fcf_to_debt@FY2024}} is the weakest of the group ({{fcf_to_debt.peer_rank@2024}}) against a median of {{fcf_to_debt.peer_median@2024}}.

snapshot.text: Groupe ADP, the Paris airport group, grew revenue by {{revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{revenue@FY2024}} in FY2024, but the EBITDA margin narrowed by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}}, the weakest of the airport peers.
Net leverage was broadly unchanged at {{net_leverage@FY2024}}, with net debt up {{net_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{net_debt@FY2024}} as capital spending rose.

The point to watch is cash generation: free cash flow fell by {{fcf.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf@FY2024}} and cash liquidity to revenue dropped by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}}.

watch_items.text: Cash generation: free cash flow fell by {{fcf.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf@FY2024}}, with FCF to debt down by {{fcf_to_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2024}}.

Investment: capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2024}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2024}}, above the peer median of {{capex_intensity.peer_median@2024}}, which keeps pressure on free cash flow.
Liquidity: cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}}, so the buffer against debt service is thinner than a year earlier.

Profitability: the EBITDA margin narrowed by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}}, the weakest of the airport peers, and impairment tests on equity-accounted holdings led to a charge.
